title: Founder File for Under-18 Hustlers
one_liner: A verified business transcript, tax pack and Roth IRA earned-income record for the parents of teens who legally can't hold the seller accounts their income runs through.
customer: Parents of 14 to 17-year-old sellers (eBay, StockX, GOAT, Whatnot, TikTok Shop, Depop, Shopify), high-school entrepreneurship programs (DECA, FBLA, Junior Achievement, NFTE), and college counselors. $12 to $15 per month or $149 per year, or $5 per student through programs.
problem: Most major marketplaces require sellers to be 18, so teens run their business under a parent's ID and account. The income, cost basis and reputation all legally belong to the parent. The parent gets a 1099-K on gross sales with no cost basis, which looks like profit. The kid can't prove any of it on a college application, and nobody is documenting the earned income that would let the family fund a custodial Roth IRA (contribution capped at the lower of earned income or the annual limit, roughly $7,000 to $7,500 per year).
solution: Founder File connects read-only to platform exports, PayPal and Gmail receipts, matches purchases to sales for cost basis, and produces: (1) a signed Business Transcript PDF for Common App activity entries and scholarship applications, (2) a Schedule C-ready summary and quarterly estimates for the parent, reviewed by a partner CPA, (3) an earned-income letter and referral to Fidelity or Schwab custodial Roth accounts, and (4) an '18th birthday migration' kit to move history to the kid's own accounts.
why_now: The 2025 tax law rolled the 1099-K reporting threshold back toward $20,000 and 200 transactions, so many teen sellers land in a confusing gray zone about reporting. College admissions increasingly reward proof of real work as test-optional policies spread and AI-polished essays get discounted. Teen commerce through TikTok Shop, Whatnot and reselling is at its peak, and Gen Alpha hustle culture is pulling younger kids in.
revenue_model: Parent subscription, per-student pricing through school programs, and referral fees from custodial brokerage accounts. Possible upsell: CPA-reviewed tax filing.
non_obvious_insight: Teen resellers are among the most under-documented earned-income earners in the country. Documenting what they already do unlocks tax-free compounding worth thousands per kid and turns a bedroom hobby into an admissions asset. The buyer is the parent, who pays for college advantage without hesitation, while everyone else sells to the kid.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 teen resellers from the Discord servers I am in. Give them free transcripts in return for parent-approved testimonials. Have a CPA friend sign off on a template. Sell a $49 'Transcript plus Roth IRA setup' bundle to their parents, and offer the transcript to 5 college-counseling and 'teen entrepreneur' TikTok creators for an affiliate cut.

title: Vacant Inherited-Home Insurance and Caretaking
one_liner: A bundled insurance-plus-sensors-plus-caretaker program for the house that sits empty during probate.
customer: Executors and heirs of a decedent's home, reached through probate attorneys, funeral homes and hospice social workers. Insurers and MGAs are the capacity partners.
problem: Homeowners policies typically restrict coverage for vandalism, freezing and other perils once a home is vacant 30-60 days, which is exactly when no probate court has appointed anyone. Probate often takes 9-18 months (unverified estimate). A burst pipe or break-in lands on an amateur executor, who may be personally exposed. Property taxes and utilities also keep running.
solution: An MGA-backed 'Estate Home Program' with a vacant-dwelling policy placed with a surplus-lines carrier, water and temperature sensors, weekly visits, lock rekeying and mail handling, utility transfer to the executor, and an optional executor advance for carrying costs repaid at sale. Add clean-out and sale-prep referrals.
why_now: Housing wealth is starting to flow from Boomers. Insurers tightened property underwriting after recent nonrenewal waves, and cheap IoT sensors make monitoring practical.
revenue_model: MGA commission (10-20%), a $150-$300/month program fee, and margin on clean-out and sale-prep referrals.
non_obvious_insight: The house effectively becomes uninsurable at the exact moment the owner dies, and nobody owns that timing gap. Executors find out after the loss.
first_30_days: Find an E&S broker who writes vacant dwellings and design a 'vacant estate' placement. Sign 5 probate attorneys and test with 10 houses. Confirm state vacancy and insurable-interest rules with a licensed agent.

title: Ghost-Student Fraud Defense for Community Colleges
one_liner: Enrollment-fraud screening built into admissions and financial-aid workflows that separates real applicants from bot-driven ghost students before aid disburses.
customer: Community-college districts' admissions, financial-aid and IT-security offices, plus state college systems. There are about 1,000 community colleges in the US.
problem: Fraud rings use stolen or synthetic identities, and increasingly AI-completed coursework, to enroll and collect federal and state aid. California community colleges have reported large shares of applications as fraudulent and tens of millions of dollars lost. Regulators have tightened identity-verification requirements for aid recipients. Staff are overwhelmed by manual reviews, and consumer IDV tools do not fit education workflows.
solution: Integrate with student information and learning management systems. Risk-score at application, enrollment and first-week activity using LMS login patterns, IP and ASN reuse, device farms, writing similarity and disbursement-account reuse. Send only high-risk cases to paid ID verification, place aid holds, produce OIG-ready reports, and give auditors a dashboard.
why_now: The 2025-26 ghost-student wave hit colleges as AI agents got good enough to attend and submit work, and aid-verification rules tightened. State funding for fraud response exists.
revenue_model: $25-100K per district per year, or $0.10-0.50 per application screened.
non_obvious_insight: The budget owner is financial-aid compliance, driven by audit findings and risk to aid eligibility, not IT. The best signals (LMS behavior) exist only after enrollment, so this is behavioral IDV that consumer vendors cannot copy.
first_30_days: Pilot with 2 colleges. Retro-score one semester of application logs to show dollars at risk, pitch through financial-aid and CIO associations, and price at $2K per month.

title: Paper-Mill Shield for Diamond Open-Access Journals
one_liner: An Open Journal Systems plugin and service that screens incoming manuscripts and reviewers using public research detectors, and hands volunteer editors a plain-language decision memo.
customer: Library-publishing programs, university presses, national journal platforms and scholarly societies that run dozens to thousands of small journals on Open Journal Systems (OJS). The buyer is the consortium or library publishing unit, not the individual journal, whose budget is close to zero.
problem: Paper mills, LLM-generated manuscripts and fake reviewer identities hit small journals run by volunteer editors. Big publishers have enterprise integrity suites (Clear Skies, the STM Integrity Hub). Small journals have nothing, and a single wave of fraudulent papers can get them delisted from Scopus or Web of Science.
solution: Submission-time screening chained from public sources: Problematic Paper Screener fingerprints (tortured phrases, ChatGPT tells), reference-list checks against the Retraction Watch database now openly available through Crossref, citation-cartel and author-network anomalies via OpenAlex, and reviewer-suggestion checks (ORCID, email domain and institution mismatches). Flagged items go to a human integrity analyst. The editor receives a one-page memo with evidence and a suggested action, not a score. Includes a backlist audit product.
why_now: Paper-mill scale is now documented (the Problematic Paper Screener scans on the order of 130M publications weekly and has fed 1,000+ retractions). Retraction Watch data went open via Crossref. LLM text makes fakes cheap. Diamond open access is growing fast because of funder mandates, which means more volunteer-run journals with no integrity budget.
revenue_model: USD 3-10 per screened submission for individual journals. Consortium plans at USD 2-15k per year covering a platform's journals. Fixed-fee backlist audits per journal. Human analyst escalations billed hourly.
non_obvious_insight: The detectors already exist as free tools used by sleuths. What editors lack is accountability packaging: a defensible written memo they can cite when rejecting an author, and someone to escalate to. Sell decision memos to the consortium that hosts the journals, not detection scores to journals.
first_30_days: Build the pipeline as a command-line tool first, then an OJS plugin. Approach three library publishing programs and the PKP community forum. Offer 5 free backlist audits to journals that consent to anonymized findings. Publish a 'state of small-journal fraud' write-up from the audits as the PR hook. Sign one consortium pilot at a nominal fee.

title: AI-Washing Forensics for Investors and Buyers
one_liner: A five-day outside-in diligence product that tests whether an AI startup's product is real autonomy, its revenue is real, and its users are human.
customer: Seed-to-growth investors (micro-VCs, corporate VCs, growth funds), corporate M&A teams, venture lenders, and enterprise procurement teams buying AI vendors.
problem: Builder.ai's 2025 insolvency (marketed AI, with heavy human labour behind it), the 2025 DOJ case against the founder of Nate, and a wave of 'ARR' made of pilots, credits and bot traffic show that diligence rests on demos, reference calls and a quality-of-earnings that never tests the technology claim.
solution: A black-box harness and data-room protocol. It covers interaction testing at scale (latency and variance signatures that reveal human-in-the-loop or third-party model calls), unit-economics reconstruction (tokens versus price versus gross margin), revenue reality (read-only Stripe and bank data plus contract sampling to separate pilot, committed, credit-funded and refunded revenue), audience authenticity (bot and agent share of users from server logs), and independent reference call-backs. Output is a 'Reality Report' with confidence intervals.
why_now: Builder.ai (2025) and Delve (2026) reset investor trust. AI-startup ARR claims are exploding, and more than half of web traffic is now automated, which inflates 'users'. Investors are compressing diligence to days, and AI products are uniquely testable from outside because you can hit the endpoint.
revenue_model: $15-40k per full report paid by the investor (often reimbursed at close), a $5k lite scan, and annual portfolio-monitoring retainers for funds.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume diligence must rely on the founder's data. AI products can be tested from the outside, so the scarce thing is independence and speed, and the buyer of speed is an investor with a 48-hour exclusivity window.
first_30_days: Offer five free 'reality scans' to angel syndicates and micro-VC partners on live deals in exchange for named case studies. Build the harness with two ML engineers and one forensic accountant. Set pricing after three wins.

title: Orphaned Solar Lease Cleanup at Home Closings
one_liner: A closing-desk service that untangles orphaned solar leases, PPAs and UCC fixture filings on retirees' homes so sales and estates can close.
customer: Title and escrow companies, listing agents, elder-law attorneys and estate executors, who pay per closing (fee taken from sale proceeds). Secondary customers are the retired homeowners themselves and their adult children.
problem: Door-to-door and telemarketed solar leases and PPAs were sold at kitchen tables to retirees on 20-25 year terms. Each one usually leaves a UCC-1 fixture filing on the home. The lessor may since have gone bankrupt (Sunnova filed Chapter 11 in June 2025 and its portfolio was sold and is now serviced by SunStrong; Mosaic and Sunlight failed earlier). Sales stall at the last minute because the buyer's lender wants the lease assumed or paid off and nobody can find the assignment chain, the current servicer or a payoff quote. Heirs inherit a lease on a dead parent's house, with monitoring dead and inverters failing. Homeowners rarely have copies of what they signed.
solution: A fixed-scope workflow. (1) Pull county and state fixture filings and reconstruct the chain of assignment. (2) Identify the current servicer and pull the contract. (3) Produce either a lender-ready transfer/assumption package with the buyer's credit-approval prep, or a payoff/buyout quote. (4) File the lien release. (5) Where the sales pitch looks deceptive or the lease unenforceable, hand off to a consumer attorney. A shared database of lessor entities, servicers and their turnaround times compounds as more closings run through it. The service is priced so title companies see it as saving their fee on a dying deal.
why_now: The Sunnova bankruptcy (filed June 2025, plan effective November 2025) created a live wave of stuck transfers, and multiple state AGs are investigating. The federal homeowner solar credit ended after 2025, pushing installers toward leases and PPAs, which let the company keep the tax credit. Leases signed in 2016-2020 are now reaching resale and probate age as the peak-65 cohort dies or downsizes.
revenue_model: Flat $750-$1,500 per closing, paid at settlement from proceeds. Title companies can take a $299/month priority-handling subscription. There is an optional buyout-negotiation success fee, and attorney referral fees where the state allows.
non_obvious_insight: The panels are not the blocker. The blocker is paperwork nobody can find: a recorded fixture filing and an assignment chain across three companies. Closers know it as the #1 surprise at the eleventh hour. Half the street signed in 2017 with a clipboard salesman and kept no copies. Whoever owns the lessor and servicer map, and the county filing pipeline, owns the unblock.
first_30_days: Pick one high-solar county in TX, FL, CA or AZ. Scrape recorded fixture filings by known lessors and cross-match them against new listings and probate filings. Call 15 title offices that have had a stuck solar closing and offer the first 3 at cost. Build template packages for the top 5 lessors and servicers. Partner with one elder-law attorney and one consumer-protection lawyer for hand-offs.

title: Referee Sampling for Black Mass and Battery Scrap
one_liner: Independent sampling and assay of black mass lots, using Pierre Gy's Theory of Sampling from mining, so scrap sellers and recyclers stop fighting over 5-15% payable swings.
customer: Battery-scrap sellers who are paid by assay: gigafactory scrap desks, EV and ESS dismantlers, and shredder pre-processors in Germany, Poland, the US Midwest, Ontario and Korea. Buyers are hydromet recyclers and trading houses that want defensible acceptance. Whoever needs the settlement pays $1.5-4k per lot or $15-40 per tonne, and often splits it.
problem: Black mass is a worst-case heterogeneous powder: coarse Cu and Al foil flakes, plastic, residual electrolyte, graphite, and a nugget effect for Ni, Co and Cu. Payables are computed on the assay of a few grams. Anyone from mining knows 90% or more of assay error is sampling error (fundamental, segregation and grouping errors), not lab error. Sellers and buyers each sample their own way and get 5-15% differences on Ni, Co and Li. Disputes are settled by splitting the difference or sending to an 'umpire' lab that repeats the same bad sampling. On a $60-150k lot, that swing is $5-15k of pure noise, paid to whoever wins the argument. The industry's chemists treat it like a homogeneous chemical.
solution: Build a containerised, safety-rated sampling and sample-prep station (dryer, rotary divider, splitter, pulverizer, inert handling) and a written ToS-based protocol: incremental sampling from a falling stream or drum auger, particle-size and moisture control, and duplicate-sample bias checks. Send splits to an accredited lab and issue a 'referee certificate' with a stated sampling variance. Provide a two-line settlement clause template that buyer and seller adopt (for example, 'referee result binds') and tie lot IDs to the recycled-content and material-recovery documentation the EU Battery Regulation requires. Extend later to PCB e-waste, catalyst scrap and mixed copper scrap.
why_now: Black mass volumes are ramping with European and US gigafactory ramp-up scrap (often 10-30% early yield loss). EU regulation is pushing black mass toward hazardous-waste treatment and export limits, and Battery Regulation recovery and recycled-content rules are phasing in. Several Western recyclers restructured or were bought out in 2025 (Li-Cycle into Glencore, for example), so sellers now fear counterparty and assay risk. Payables have become the main margin lever as Co and Ni prices swing.
revenue_model: Per-lot referee fee ($1.5-4k) or $15-40 per tonne, annual retainers for large scrap generators, leasing or operating sample-prep stations at recycler gates, and certification and training for recyclers' in-house sampling.
non_obvious_insight: The fight looks like an assay-accuracy problem but it is a sampling problem, and the solution is 1950s-1990s sampling theory that only mining and metallurgy people internalise. Recycling companies are staffed by chemists and process engineers who sample like it is a solution. A person who has been burned by a bad grade-control sample sees the whole market as one giant unsampled stockpile.
first_30_days: Rent time on a commercial sample-prep lab or buy used splitting and pulverizing gear (about $40-60k). Offer a free duplicate-sampling study to three scrap generators or dismantlers: take 10 lots, sample each with the seller's method and yours, and send blind splits to two labs. Show them the between-protocol bias, then sell a 6-month referee retainer. A local mining-lab partner and one senior sampling consultant give instant credibility.

title: Deferred-Payment Shield for Grain Sellers
one_liner: A counterparty-risk monitor plus surety/letter-of-credit wrap that turns the unsecured December 'deferred payment' loans farmers unknowingly make to their elevators into protected receivables.
customer: Row-crop operators with 2,000+ acres who each defer $400k to $2M of grain revenue into January, and the ag lenders and farm CPAs who advise them. Co-ops and elevators with strong balance sheets are a secondary payer, because the wrap becomes a way to win bushels.
problem: Every November and December, farmers sign deferred payment contracts to push income into next year for tax reasons. Most think they are just delaying a check. Legally, title has passed and they are unsecured creditors of the buyer. Iowa's Grain Indemnity Fund gives deferred payment contracts zero coverage. Deferred pricing ('price later') contracts get 75% coverage capped at $400,000 per claimant. Farm balance sheets are stretched, so more farmers are lending large sums to buyers they have never vetted.
solution: Start with a free 'Elevator Exposure Report'. The farmer lists every open contract, prepaid input balance and stored-grain receipt. The tool compares total exposure with the Fund's actual coverage and scores each buyer using licensing status, audit history, buyer size, and settlement-timing behavior reported by users. Then sell the fix. A specialty MGA or bank issues a surety bond or standby letter of credit against the buyer's payment promise, structured with ag tax counsel so tax deferral is preserved. The fee is roughly 0.3% to 0.8% of face value. Ag lenders subscribe to a portfolio dashboard showing how much of their borrowers' grain receivables sit with weak buyers.
why_now: Chapter 12 farm bankruptcies rose 46% in 2025 and April 2026 hit a six-year high. USDA projects record farm debt of about $625B in 2026. The 2025 bumper crop and low prices pushed farmers toward deferral and storage. The 2026 December deferral season opens in about 90 days, which is a hard deadline for a first pilot.
revenue_model: Wrap fee split with the surety or LC provider (0.3% to 0.8% of contract face value). Ag lender portfolio-monitoring subscription ($1k to $5k a month per lender). Optional $299 per farm annual exposure audit sold through CPAs.
non_obvious_insight: The elevator that pushes deferred payment contracts hardest in November is often the one that needs your cash, because deferrals are free working capital for a thinly capitalized buyer. Farmers think of the elevator as a warehouse. Once title passes, it is a borrower. Nobody rates that borrower.
first_30_days: Build the exposure calculator as a free web form and scorecard from Iowa Dept. of Ag license data and public filings. Get 5 farm CPAs and 3 rural banks to run their biggest clients through it. Sign one surety broker or bank willing to quote wraps, and target 10 paid wraps before the December deferral rush.

title: Recipient-Priced Inboxes for Outbound Agents
one_liner: A gateway that lets busy people set a price to reach them and makes outbound AI agents bid for attention, refunding the bond when the message proves relevant.
customer: Outbound agents (fundraising, PR, recruiting sourcing, partnership and research-interview agents) that decide per message whether a reply is worth $1-$50 and pay a refundable bond. The recipient side is VC partners, journalists, podcast bookers, specialist physicians and procurement heads.
problem: Agents remove the cost of sending, so high-value inboxes are drowning. Generic AI outreach now gets under 1% replies in most B2B segments, and reaching one buyer takes 7+ touches. Filters are an arms race, and recipients earn nothing for their attention.
solution: The recipient sets a price ladder (for example $5 for a read-guarantee, $25 for a reply window) and rules. Unknown senders get an auto-reply, or an HTTP 402 for agents, carrying a payment link. The sender agent estimates expected value from its own conversion data and posts a refundable bond over MPP, x402 or card. With one tap the recipient marks the message relevant, which returns the bond, or irrelevant, which pays the recipient. We take 15-20% of forfeited bonds. Sender reputation lowers prices for good senders and prices out spammers.
why_now: Agentic outbound exploded in 2026, with agents choosing targets and follow-ups on their own and degrading deliverability. Programmatic micropayment rails now make a $2 bond collectible without a human. Recipients are actively looking for ways to filter AI outreach.
revenue_model: 15-20% of forfeited bonds plus a 5% fee on settled reads. Team-inbox and executive-assistant tiers for recipients, and an API plan for senders that want reputation scores.
non_obvious_insight: Pay-to-email has failed for 25 years because humans underprice their own outreach and hate friction. Agents compute expected value per message, so a price signal finally clears the market, and it only works when both sides are software. Letting the recipient earn money flips their incentive from blocking to hosting.
first_30_days: Build a Gmail and Chrome extension with an auto-reply rule and recruit 50 investors, journalists and podcast bookers through founder networks. Recruit 10 outbound-agent tools (fundraising, PR, recruiting) as senders. Settle bonds manually via Stripe at first and measure reply-quality uplift against free outreach. Charge the take rate from month 2.

title: Insider-Trading Watchdog for Entertainment Announcements
one_liner: Sportradar-style integrity monitoring for game publishers, studios and awards bodies whose announcements and results now trade as prediction-market contracts.
customer: Legal and compliance teams at game publishers, film and TV studios, awards bodies, esports leagues and streamers. Prediction-market exchanges are a secondary buyer.
problem: Kalshi valuation went from about $11B to $22B between Dec 2025 and May 2026, and entertainment and awards are already about 11% of activity. Employees, agencies, vendors and journalists under embargo hold non-public information that now has a price. No one monitors it, and sports leagues already pay for integrity services that entertainment lacks.
solution: Map every listed contract on Kalshi, Polymarket and other venues to the client's titles, awards and announcements. Detect abnormal volume and price moves ahead of reveals, and deliver incident packets for counsel. Add embargo-tier employee policy and training, and give exchanges a restricted-list API.
why_now: Prediction markets are expanding beyond sports despite state fights, and regulators will demand integrity partners as entertainment contracts multiply.
revenue_model: $2-10k per month subscriptions for IP owners, exchange-side API fees, and forensic investigations at project rates.
non_obvious_insight: Publishers think prediction markets are a gambling issue for someone else. For the first time, their 5,000 employees and 300 vendors hold embargoed information worth money. Sports solved this with third-party integrity vendors, and entertainment has none.
first_30_days: Build a tracker of all entertainment and gaming contracts across major venues. Publish a report on volume spikes before announcements. Contact compliance heads at 10 publishers and awards bodies, and sell one 3-month pilot at $5k per month.

title: Dead-Lead Exchange for Solar Installers
one_liner: A reason-coded exchange where solar installers sell their disqualified leads (bad roof, shade, small panel) to roofers, arborists and electricians, with a bounty when the homeowner comes back to buy solar.
customer: Roofers, tree services and panel-upgrade electricians pay per lead. Solar installers receive a revenue share and are the supply side. The end payer is the trade at $60-150 per lead, plus a 5-10% bounty from the installer when a returned lead signs.
problem: Installers pay $100-250 for an exclusive lead and $150-800 for a booked appointment, and CAC is reportedly rising about 40% in 2026. Most of the spend dies at qualification on roof age, shade, roof type or a 100A panel, and the lead is thrown away or resold as an aged inquiry. Meanwhile roofers pay hundreds per closed lead for homeowners who may not need a roof at all.
solution: Installers connect their CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, JobNimbus, Enerflo) through a webhook. Every lead tagged with a disqualification reason goes to the exchange. A fresh, named-trade consent step, by SMS or a call, offers the homeowner a free quote from a local roofer to make the house solar-ready. The exchange sells the lead to a matched local trade with the diagnosis attached: roof age, photos, shade map, utility bill. When the work completes, the lead returns to the original installer with a 90-day exclusive hold, and the installer pays a bounty if it closes.
why_now: After 25D expired, installers are fighting over unit economics and CAC is climbing, so recouping 30-50% of lead cost matters. Roofers face slower storm work. Homeowners still want solar through TPO, which typically requires 10-15+ years of roof life, so more leads get rejected on roof grounds.
revenue_model: Take 50-60% of the lead price with the rest shared with the installer. Add a 5-10% bounty on returned solar sales. Add a per-seat subscription for roofing and tree companies to get first look in their zip codes. Later, add a financing product that bundles a roof and solar into one loan.
non_obvious_insight: The dead solar lead is one of the best roofing leads in the county. This is a homeowner who was ready to commit five figures to their house, has shown a utility bill, and has just been told by a credible outsider that the roof needs work, so the diagnosis is trusted. VCs treat lead-gen as a commodity, but a closed loop with bounce-back and reason codes is not. The compliance layer (fresh, named-trade consent) is the moat.
first_30_days: Sign 3 installers in one metro who each have 200+ disqualified leads a month. Recruit 3 roofers and 1-2 tree services. Run the whole loop with a spreadsheet, SMS consent scripts and Stripe payouts. Price the first leads at $75-100. Track lead-to-roof-job conversion and how many come back to solar.

title: Dumpster-Drop Leads for the Next Trade
angle: Pairing 2: Construction/housing shortage/trades labor/home services x Waste/recycling/circular economy/critical minerals/materials
one_liner: A white-label booking flow for independent roll-off dumpster companies that sells the homeowner's renovation start as an exclusive, unshared lead to the next trade in sequence.
customer: Local electricians, plumbers, drywall and paint, flooring and roofing shops pay per exclusive lead. Independent roll-off haulers (10-40 trucks) get revenue share and better booking software.
problem: 73% of homeowners have unstarted projects, 78% of them have no quotes, and the barriers are 'too busy' (21%), trust (21%) and no response (14%). Homeowner-plus-pro jobs rose from 27% to 46% while DIY-only fell from 50% to 39%. Angi charges $15-85 per lead and resells each to many bidders, and about 48% of home-service calls never reach a person.
solution: When a homeowner books a 10-30 yard bin, a two-question flow captures project type, timing, budget and lead-sharing consent. The hauler recommends one pre-vetted pro for the next step (electrical rough-in after demo, flooring after tear-out), with no bidding. The pro pays $50-120 only for an accepted lead. Drivers confirm project stage at swap-outs.
why_now: The DIY-plus-pro shift makes the demo-and-haul step the natural first purchase. Distrust of shared-lead marketplaces is high, and cheap AI text and voice booking lets small haulers add a lead flow without staff. Median home age is 44 years and remodeling spend hit a record $524B.
revenue_model: Per exclusive lead, about 40% shared with the hauler; SaaS for haulers at $99-299/mo; a recycled-C&D upsell.
non_obvious_insight: The dumpster is the earliest hard commitment in a remodel: money is spent and demo starts within days. The hauler is a locally trusted, neutral party that sees demand before any contractor quotes it. Its leads are exclusive, which is the opposite of Angi's economics.
first_30_days: Sign 3 independent haulers in one metro. Add consent and project questions to their web and phone booking. Recruit 6 pros (one per trade) at about $60 per exclusive lead. Measure booking-to-job conversion for a month and tune the trade sequence before adding metros.

title: Side-Selling Early Warning for Milk and Coffee Coops
one_liner: A churn-prediction and targeted-advance service that tells dairy and coffee cooperatives which farmers are about to side-sell to cash brokers, and triggers the right cash intervention before the volume walks away.
customer: Managers and boards of medium-sized dairy cooperatives (about 2,000-10,000 farmers), coffee cooperative societies and factories, and mid-sized processors that buy from farmer groups. They pay because lost throughput hits fixed factory costs and credit recovery.
problem: Side-selling is the silent killer of Kenyan coops. Farmers sell milk to hawkers and raw-milk traders, or coffee cherry to cash buyers, who pay on the spot, while the coop pays monthly or later and then deducts for feeds, inputs, AI services and loans. Deliveries fade slowly, not suddenly, so managers notice too late. Side-selling spikes when a farmer's net pay is squeezed by deductions, when payment is late, or in cash-crunch weeks such as January and other school fee dates, funerals and sickness. Coops respond with lectures and warnings instead of predicting and fixing the cash gap.
solution: Ingest the coop's delivery and payment history (usually already exported from the weighing or dairy management software). A simple gradient-boosted or rule-based model scores each farmer weekly for side-selling risk using delivery drift, missed pay days, deductions as a share of gross, days since last payment, seasonality and school-term calendars. The coop gets a daily short list for its field officer, with SMS or voice-call scripts in the local language. The intervention is a coop-funded, capped advance or deduction holiday for at-risk farmers in their predicted cash-crunch window, since the coop already holds the delivered stock and the farmer's record as collateral. It measures recovered litres or kilos against a control group.
why_now: Global arabica prices spiked to record highs in 2025 and pulled cherry towards cash brokers in Kenya, at the same time as coffee-sector reforms push coops to pay faster and more transparently. Weighing scales and dairy management software have digitised delivery data at many coops over the last five years, so the data now exists. M-Pesa bulk disbursement makes weekly or on-demand advances cheap. Modern ML tooling makes a credible model a two-week job rather than a research project. I could not verify current legal specifics, so confirm the latest coffee and dairy regulations and data-protection obligations (coop as data controller) before pilots.
revenue_model: Performance fee of roughly 5-10% of recovered volume value (paid from the additional milk or cherry that stays in the coop), or a SaaS retainer of a few tens of thousands of shillings per month per coop. Later, licensing the model to processors and lenders who want a farmer reliability signal.
non_obvious_insight: Side-selling is not disloyalty, it is a rational response to cash-flow timing. The winning intervention is not a scolding letter but a small advance placed at the right moment, funded by the coop's own working capital. It is also predictable from delivery patterns weeks before it happens, because farmers taper deliveries before they stop. Most agritech sells farmers new products, whereas here the buyer is the institution that quietly loses 10% or more of its volume.
first_30_days: Get 24 months of delivery and payment CSVs from one or two coops, ideally through your own parents' society or the manager you know personally. Build the risk model in a notebook, deliver a top-200 at-risk list plus a script, and run a 60-day test where half the list gets the SMS and advance offer and half does not. Agree to be paid only on retained volume compared to the control group, and use the result as the case study for the next five coops.

title: AI Kill-Switch Drills That Unlock Affirmative Cover
one_liner: A third-party 'shutdown drill' and evidence certificate proving a company can halt its AI systems fast, so carriers will write affirmative AI cover and insureds can qualify for it.
customer: Mid-market companies (50-2,000 staff) running customer-facing or agentic AI, paying $4-12k per year. Their cyber and E&O brokers and MGAs are secondary payers, at a per-verified-insured fee.
problem: Admitted carriers are adding AI exclusions to general liability and E&O while specialty carriers sell narrow affirmative AI add-ons. Buyers cannot show underwriters that they can stop a misbehaving AI system, so they either go uncovered or pay E&S prices.
solution: A quarterly 'AI shutdown drill'. We inventory the client's AI systems and agents, run a timed kill-switch and rollback test with a runbook, and log the evidence. We issue a carrier-readable attestation, modeled on how MFA and EDR scans became underwriting inputs, with the API and PDF formats brokers can attach to submissions. Carriers and MGAs get standardized control data for pricing AI endorsements.
why_now: Beazley announced an 'industry-first' AI Voluntary Shutdown endorsement on 2026-09-25. CFC is embedding affirmative AI wording across its portfolio (2026-09-24). Insurers are debating targeted exclusions for systemic AI events and for autonomous decisions made 'as designed' (2026-08-31). Affirmative AI cover is only now shipping, and its triggers depend on shutdown capability nobody yet verifies.
revenue_model: Annual drill subscription of $4-12k per insured. Per-attestation fees of $250-500 paid by MGAs and carriers, or a revenue share on AI endorsements that bind with a certificate attached. A later data licence to carriers.
non_obvious_insight: Demand is visible in insurer behavior. Surplus lines coverage is described as filling in where admitted carriers are 'implementing the best, most absolute AI exclusions and limiting coverage in traditional general liability policies' (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2026/09/23/886403.htm). Beazley's new AI Voluntary Shutdown and AI Regulatory Defence endorsements pay to suspend a malfunctioning AI system (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2026/09/25/886788.htm). Travelers' risk index finds 89% of businesses use AI daily but only 59% have employee AI-use practices, so a verification gap exists (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2026/09/23/886527.htm). Insurers are discussing exclusions for AI models causing correlated losses and for agents acting autonomously (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2026/08/31/883343.htm). Cyber insurance took off once controls became verifiable and discountable, and the same will happen for AI. The scarce asset is neutral proof of a control, not another AI policy-analysis tool.
first_30_days: Write a one-page shutdown-drill standard covering agents, model-vendor kill paths, rollback and comms. Recruit 3 cyber brokers to nominate 10 pilot clients. Run 5 free drills to build case studies, then approach 2 MGAs or carriers already selling affirmative AI cover (CFC and Beazley are the visible ones) with the sample attestation. Charge from drill number 6 and close the first 3 paying clients through broker channels.

title: Court-Ready Deepfake Authenticity Reports for Lawyers
one_liner: $500-1,500, 48-hour forensic reports on disputed audio, video, screenshots and voicemails, written to survive an authenticity challenge.
customer: Solo and small family-law, employment and criminal-defence firms, insurer special-investigation units, and HR investigators.
problem: Cloned-voice voicemails and fabricated chats now appear in custody and harassment disputes. The proposed federal evidence rules on deepfakes (901(c)) and machine-generated evidence (707) have stalled, and in June 2026 the Standing Committee sent 707 back for further study, so judges decide case by case. Bespoke forensic experts cost $5-20k and take weeks.
solution: A productised workflow: intake with chain of custody, multiple detectors plus provenance checks (metadata, C2PA, compression history, device and source-app fingerprints), review and a signed declaration from a credentialed examiner, optional testimony, and template motions on authentication for lawyers.
why_now: Cheap voice cloning has moved from fraud into family and employment disputes. The federal rule process has stalled, leaving a gap that judges and lawyers must fill with experts, and lawyers face sanctions if they present unverified AI evidence.
revenue_model: $500-1,500 per report, $2-5k per day for testimony, and a $299 per month firm plan that includes three reports.
non_obvious_insight: Detection accuracy is weak everywhere. The scarce thing is a credentialed human willing to sign under oath with a documented method. Productise the signature and the paper trail, and treat detectors as inputs.
first_30_days: Recruit three forensic audio and video examiners. Sell through local family-law bar associations and CLE talks. Publish three anonymised case studies and a report template reviewed by trial attorneys.

title: Retired Operators as Fractional Rural Water Chiefs
angle: Pairing 1: Aging/eldercare/silver economy x Water scarcity/infrastructure
one_liner: A cooperative of retired licensed water operators, each serving as the certified 'operator in responsible charge' for several tiny water systems remotely plus monthly visits, while converting their tacit knowledge into digital manuals.
customer: Small community water systems under about 3,300 people (councils, water districts, mobile-home park owners, county utilities). State rural water associations and engineering firms refer them. Each pays a $2.5-5k/month retainer.
problem: About a third of the water workforce is eligible to retire within a decade, and tiny systems cannot compete for certified operators. No software fixes 'nobody with a license answers the phone at 2 a.m.' PFAS initial monitoring is due in 2027, the lead action level tightens to 0.010 mg/L on Nov 1, 2027, and nitrate hits small farm-belt systems hardest. Meanwhile 60-72-year-old operators want part-time income, autonomy and purpose.
solution: Recruit retirees holding Grade 2-4 certifications. Each covers 3-5 systems using remote SCADA and camera access, a compliance calendar (sampling, PFAS monitoring, lead-inventory reporting, consumer confidence reports) and a shared on-call rotation inside the co-op. Every operator records an 'exit interview' that becomes site-specific SOPs (which valve sticks, which well drops in August). A young apprentice is attached to each cluster so succession is built in. The co-op keeps 25-30%.
why_now: 2027 PFAS and lead-rule deadlines are close, and $7.2B of FY2026 State Revolving Fund money flows to systems that must show capable operations. Boomer retirements are peaking. Federal technical capacity is shrinking (EPA's research office was eliminated in 2026), and small systems are left on their own.
revenue_model: $2.5-5k per system per month retainer, of which the co-op keeps 25-30% and the operator earns roughly $30-50k a year part-time. One-off compliance projects (PFAS sampling programs, lead service line inventories) add $5-20k each.
non_obvious_insight: Tiny systems do not need 'AI SCADA'. They need one accountable licensed human, and the only growing supply of licensed operators is retirees. Many states let one certified operator be in responsible charge of several small systems (rules vary by state and need checking). The retiree's tacit local knowledge is the real asset being lost.
first_30_days: Partner with the state Rural Water Association and get the drinking-water program's list of systems with operator-certification violations. Recruit 8 retired operators through the association newsletter and conference. Sign 3 systems on 90-day trial retainers.

title: Sleep-Apnea-to-GLP-1 Pathway for DME Suppliers
one_liner: A co-management service that lets sleep labs and CPAP suppliers prescribe, retest and retain patients as they lose weight.
customer: Independent sleep centers, home-sleep-test companies and DME suppliers whose profit engine is CPAP resupply.
problem: Zepbound was approved for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity on Dec 20, 2024, and Part D can cover it for OSA. As weight falls, patients drop CPAP without a retest or re-titration, and the DME loses resupply revenue and the patient. Sleep clinics have no pathway for prescribing or co-managing a drug.
solution: Baseline and 3/6/12-month home sleep tests, benefits verification and prior authorization for Zepbound-for-OSA, a nutrition and muscle plan, auto-CPAP pressure re-titration from device data, and a 'retest before you quit CPAP' protocol. DMEs keep the supply relationship where still needed.
why_now: The OSA indication now has Medicare and commercial coverage routes, and cash pricing is falling, so patient demand is arriving at sleep clinics without a pathway. DMEs see the threat and hold the patient data (CPAP usage) needed to co-manage.
revenue_model: $15-30 per patient per month to the DME or sleep center, or a share of retained resupply, plus per-test fees.
non_obvious_insight: The DME supplier looks like the loser but is the natural gatekeeper: it has adherence data, patient trust and a recurring billing relationship, and it will pay to convert lost resupply into a managed weight-and-airway program.
first_30_days: Approach 5 regional DMEs or sleep centers. Pilot on 100 CPAP patients with BMI of 30 or more and AHI of 15 or more. Measure PA success, retest rate and retained resupply.

title: Restock Monitors Turned Competitor Sell-Through Radar
one_liner: Repurpose the Discord restock-monitor infrastructure teen resellers run into a SKU- and size-level sell-through index for DTC brands and the investors and acquirers who buy them.
customer: Founders and merchandisers of DTC brands who want to see rivals' sell-through ($199 to $799 per month), boutique retail buyers, and consumer-focused funds, search-fund buyers and e-commerce acquirers who need diligence on a Shopify brand ($2,000 to $5,000 per report).
problem: Everyone in e-commerce has to guess how fast a competitor's hero product actually sells. Public analytics tools give traffic estimates, not sell-through by size, color or restock. Buyers of small Shopify brands take the seller's word for 'we sell out in days' and get burned.
solution: Teen resellers already run monitors on thousands of storefronts: each one polls public product feeds so a Discord ping fires the instant a size restocks. The same stream, kept as history, shows how fast each variant flips to sold-out, restock cadence, drop timing, markdown timing, price changes and collection moves. Package it as a weekly Sold-Out Index and an on-demand brand report: 'their black M hoodie sold out in 41 minutes twice, restocked every 3 weeks, and they cut price 15% after the tariff news'. Use public storefront signals only, with no checkout tricks, and honor rate limits and terms.
why_now: Tariff-driven price changes in 2025-26 have every brand asking what rivals did to prices and when. DTC brand acquisition and roll-up activity means more diligence is being done on tiny Shopify brands. LLMs now classify messy product titles into a clean taxonomy cheaply, which was the hard part of turning monitor pings into an index.
revenue_model: Subscription for brand and retail buyers ($199 to $799 per month), one-off diligence reports ($2,000 to $5,000), and a data feed for funds later.
non_obvious_insight: The restock-alert economy is really an accidental, huge, always-on sensor network for the long tail of DTC commerce. Enterprise alt-data vendors ignore small brands because they think there is no data on them. Resellers have been logging exactly that data every minute for years. The unit of value is sold-out speed by variant, which reseller monitors track and analytics vendors do not.
first_30_days: Take the existing monitor feed for about 2,000 storefronts in streetwear, sneakers and collectibles and start logging history now, because history is the asset. Publish a free weekly Sold-Out Index thread on TikTok and X to get inbound. Sell 10 founders a $199 competitor watchlist by DM. Pitch one search-fund or acquirer community for a paid diligence report at $2,000 to check willingness to pay.

title: Broker Non-Payment Bond-Claim Collective for Small Carriers
one_liner: A service that files carriers' unpaid-load claims against the broker's surety bond and FMCSA record, pools every claimant against the same broker, and publishes a real days-to-pay broker score built from actual payment outcomes.
customer: Small carriers and owner-operators (1 to 10 trucks), including hot-shot and box-truck carriers who don't factor every load. A second revenue stream comes from carriers who pay to check brokers before hauling.
problem: Small unpaid loads are too small for a lawyer and too big to shrug off. One carrier reported a $600 CAD load completed in November 2025 still unpaid in June 2026, after 50+ emails and calls that got only automated replies from a 'Legal Dispute Department'. Their workaround was to 'sign up with factoring companies' who 'either approve or deny'. Meanwhile freight rates have stayed squeezed since 2022, so broker failures and slow payers keep coming.
solution: The carrier uploads the rate confirmation, proof of delivery and invoice. The service verifies the broker's authority and bond or trust-fund status from public FMCSA data, sends a formal demand, and files the claim with the broker's surety (federal rules require property brokers to carry financial security, at $75,000, which is paid out pro rata when many claimants exist). It files an FMCSA complaint and logs every step. The key mechanic is pooling: claims against the same broker are grouped so its claimants are first in line and can cite a pattern. All outcomes feed a broker pay-speed database ('median days to pay', 'claims filed', 'claims paid') that carriers check before booking a load. A trucking attorney reviews templates to stay clear of unauthorized-practice issues.
why_now: The freight recession is still going: the owner-operator thread 'Rates are crashing and fuel to the moon!' began in March 2022 and was on page 1,134 as of Sept 26, 2026. Squeezed brokers pay slowly or fail, and forums are full of fraud and non-payer alerts. Document-heavy claim filing can now be automated cheaply. Factoring companies increasingly reject unknown or slow brokers, which pushes more risk back to unfactored small carriers.
revenue_model: 20 to 25% contingency on recovered amounts. A $15 per month subscription for broker pay-speed lookups and alerts. Later, sell the broker payment-behavior data to factoring companies and load boards.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not the collection letter but the payment-behavior data no credit bureau has, and it is created only by filing claims in bulk. The owner of one 'fraud alert' thread described 50+ emails and only automated replies over 7 months for a $600 CAD load, with a second victim in the same thread and factoring as the only workaround (https://www.thetruckersreport.com/truckingindustryforum/posts/13536421/). The margin squeeze is ongoing: the rates-and-fuel thread reached page 1,134 in Sept 2026 (https://www.thetruckersreport.com/truckingindustryforum/posts/13542683/). A new-authority owner-operator says he cannot get financing and rents a box truck by the day, missing about $4,000 a day in loads, which shows how thin small carriers' cash is (https://www.thetruckersreport.com/truckingindustryforum/posts/13465676/). The bond rule detail is from general knowledge of FMCSA broker financial-security requirements and needs legal confirmation.
first_30_days: Week 1: recruit a trucking attorney to review one claim template. Post in the TruckersReport Freight Broker forum offering free claim filing to carriers in the fraud-alert threads. Weeks 2 to 3: file 15 to 20 claims by hand, group them by broker, and record response times. Week 4: publish the first 'days-to-pay' leaderboard of 25 brokers, and start charging 20% contingency. Target: 30 claims filed and 5 paid, with the leaderboard as the top-of-funnel.

title: Same-Day Sub and Coach Bench for Home Daycares
angle: Pairing 2: Mental health, loneliness and community x Parenting, childcare deserts and kids/AI/screens
one_liner: A membership that guarantees a licensed home daycare a vetted substitute within hours and, when a child's behavior threatens expulsion, an on-call early-childhood coach, so licensed slots stay open and parents keep their jobs.
customer: Licensed family child care providers (solo operators; start with about 300 in one metro or state). Co-payers: state agencies and child-care resource and referral (CCR&R) organizations with workforce-support funds, employers buying backup-care value, and Head Start partners.
problem: Childcare deserts are as much a retention problem as a construction problem. Family homes were the fastest-growing supply (+4.3% in 2024, versus +1.5% for centers), but one sick day closes a solo business, providers work 50-60 hour weeks, and average childcare worker pay is $33,140. Behavior challenges lead to expulsions, and few early-childhood mental health consultants exist to help. Each lost slot means a parent leaves work.
solution: 1) 'Slot Guarantee': a bench of background-checked, trained substitutes (retired teachers, early-education students, displaced parents) dispatched via app on a 2-hour target. 2) 'Calm Team': early-childhood coaches supervised by an infant-mental-health-endorsed clinician, deployed for observation and a behavior plan before expulsion. 3) Monthly Provider Circles of about 8 providers for peer support and reflective supervision. 4) Light back-office (attendance, billing).
why_now: Employer and family demand for childcare is rising with the 45F credit (40-50%) and the $7,500 dependent-care FSA, but supply is thin and fragile. Family homes are the growth segment, so protecting them is the cheapest new capacity. States are already funding workforce supports and early-childhood mental health consultation.
revenue_model: Provider membership of $79-129/mo including a few sub days per quarter, with extra sub hours billed at about $22/hr plus a fee. State or CCR&R contracts per provider. Behavior-coach visits at about $150 each or covered by state mental health consultation funds. Employer backup-care pools.
non_obvious_insight: Every desert plan builds new slots. The cheaper win is stopping existing slots from closing over sick days, burnout and expulsions. The real unit of childcare supply is a provider's mental state, and support for it is a bench of people, not an app.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 providers in one metro through Facebook groups and a CCR&R newsletter with a $59 founding-member rate. Assemble 15 substitutes from retired teachers and early-education students. Partner with one infant-mental-health clinician to lead the first Provider Circles. Approach the local CCR&R or county for a pilot fund, and track closures avoided as the headline metric.
